sentences.text: In the memo, dated 18.04.2023, filed by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant seeking withdrawal of the appeal, it is stated that the Execution Petition No.44/2022 on the file of Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Shiggaon, is settled vide order dated 11.02.2023 passed by the Lok Adalat.

Further, the appellant had also made prayer to refund the statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- made before this Court and for withdrawal of Rs.1,00,000/- deposited in terms of the interim order granted by this Court.
Accordingly, the prayer was granted.
And the order was not signed.

Hence,
the said order is recalled.
3. The order dismissing the appeal as withdrawn was passed at 10.30 a.m., on a mention made by the learned counsel for the appellant.

The case was listed at Sl.No.52 in the cause list, and obviously,
the counsel for the respondents/claimants was not present before the Court.

Later, on the same day,
the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants brought to the notice of the Court that the appeal is withdrawn without notice to the respondents/claimants and without disclosing the details of the alleged compromise arrived at by the parties in the execution proceedings and requested that the matter be listed today.
Accordingly, the matter is listed today.

4. Sri. K.H.Bagi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that a copy of the compromise petition said to have been filed in Execution Petition No.44/2022 before the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Shiggaon.
This Court has perused the said compromise petition.
It is stated in the compromise petition that the claimants have agreed to receive Rs.50,000/- towards full and final settlement of their claim.
5. This Court has also perused the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,04,280/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The amount agreed upon under the compromise is less than what is deposited before this Court.

It is also forthcoming from the compromise petition, which is now presented today, that the signature of the parties are not found on each page of the compromise petition, particularly, on the pages containing the terms of the compromise petition of alleged settlement.
The signatures are found only on the last two pages which do not contain any condition relating to settlement.
6. Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants submits that he will take appropriate steps to question the correctness of the compromise accepted by the Lok Adalat, Shiggaon.

7. Under these circumstances, this Court deems it appropriate to pass the following order:
"The appellant is permitted to withdraw the appeal.

However, the amount of Rs.1,25,000/- deposited before this Court shall continue to be in deposit for a period of two months till the respondents takes appropriate action relating to the alleged compromise accepted by the Lok Adalat, Shiggaon.
If no action is initiated within two months, the amount in deposit shall be released in favour of the appellant."
